Overview: Varicose veins are enlarged, twisted veins that most often appear in the legs because weakened vein valves allow blood to pool instead of flowing efficiently back to the heart. They can cause discomfort, heaviness, and cosmetic concerns, and in some cases may lead to skin changes or ulcers if left untreated.
Symptoms: Twisted or bulging blue veins in the legs, aching or heavy legs, swelling that worsens after long standing, itching over the veins, muscle cramps, and skin discoloration around the ankles.
Causes: Varicose veins commonly develop when vein walls or valves become weak. Risk factors include prolonged standing, pregnancy, obesity, aging, family history, and reduced physical activity.
Preventions: Maintain a healthy weight, stay physically active, avoid standing or sitting for very long periods, elevate your legs when resting, and consider compression stockings if recommended by a clinician.
Treatment: Treatment may include compression stockings, exercise, weight management, leg elevation, and medical procedures such as sclerotherapy, laser treatment, or other vein procedures when symptoms are significant.
When to See a Doctor: See a doctor if you develop persistent pain, worsening swelling, skin ulcers, bleeding from a vein, sudden redness or warmth, or if leg symptoms interfere with daily activities.
